name: Still Human // Wild
description: The spin-off of Still Human, with the walls taken off. Five hundred and seventy-six metres of hand-pressed clay country, streamed in as you walk it: plains, a river running the length of the map, mountain ranges with snow on them, and seven kilns. One is yours from the start. Two are living settlements with a bench and a board of work. Four are dead, held by a blight that daylight will not shift, and relighting one makes its ring, its bench and its safe ground yours. Look at a tree, a boulder or a clay bank and hold the button: a ring fills and it comes up in one piece, faster and richer once you have made an axe and a pick. Sculpt the hill into a shape you meant, raise a house out of brick, thatch, timber, cut stone, kiln glass and lantern light, and spend the rest on the Kiln itself: a wider ring, fed braziers, a taller tower, a better bench. A chain of objectives names the next thing and marks it on the map; a contract board at every lit settlement pays for the work you would rather do instead. After dark the ground gives up husks, stalkers, lumberers, emberwisps and molders, and every one of them leaves a weapon or a piece of plate on the grass before it goes. Third person over the shoulder, stop-motion at twelve frames a second, and the world you changed is still changed when you come back.

inputs.description: The resident — read from the shell so the valley is filed under the same name you use everywhere else in the hub.

outputs.description: The valley itself — seed, day count, every cell of terrain you raised or lowered, every block you placed, which trees, boulders and clay banks are gone, which kilns are lit and what still holds the rest, your place in the chain of objectives, the contracts in hand, the Kiln's upgrade levels, your tools and your kit. Written on leaving and every twenty-two seconds, so a run survives the window closing.

author: Present Palm
